cases.customer_question: What should be done when Bluetooth SIG identifies a product as potentially unqualified but the company believes it may have been registered in the past?
cases.actual_issue: A suspected qualification violation was investigated and later resolved when Bluetooth SIG located an older EPL-era qualification record that was not visible through normal modern searches. The real issue became ownership and account control of the historical registration.
cases.plain_english_explanation: A company thought a product might never have been qualified. After investigation, SIG found an older qualification record. The challenge was not creating a new qualification but recovering access and ownership of the existing qualification history.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant interpreted the SIG response as evidence that a historical EPL qualification already existed. Instead of creating a new membership or repeating qualification work, the company should create an individual SIG account and request transfer of the historical Listing Owner responsibilities. The enforcement issue was ultimately resolved because the qualification record already existed.
cases.decision_logic: When a valid historical EPL registration exists, the preferred path is to establish ownership and control of that registration rather than duplicate qualification activities.
cases.final_recommendation: Search for historical qualification records, create the necessary SIG user account, and submit a Listing Owner transfer request when legacy registrations are found.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: A company may perform unnecessary qualification work, create duplicate records, or fail to resolve enforcement actions despite already having valid historical qualification evidence.
